How IFM uses it (build.py --codec=zip, the default):
  * build.py packs the stripped Lua sources into one ZIP (ZIP_DEFLATED, level 9) and
    embeds it as base64 inside ifm_bundle.lua: local __IFM_ARCHIVE = table.concat({...}).
  * The bundle decodes that base64 and hands the ZIP bytes to the vendored zzlib:
    zzlib.files() iterates the entries, zzlib.unzip(buf, offset, crc) inflates each packed
    entry (CRC32 verified) and the unpacker writes ./ifm/** with the usual write rules.
  * No upstream file is modified. zzlib's require("inflate-bit32") is answered by an injected
    local require() that returns the vendored inflate-bit32 chunk, so no filesystem
    require/package lookup happens on the CC:T side (_VERSION is irrelevant there).
  * inflate-bit32 uses bit32 (Lua 5.2) / bit (LuaJIT). There is no fallback any more: a
    runtime that provides neither aborts the unpack with an explicit assert (see
    VENDOR_PRELUDE in build.py).

Updating: fetch both files again, refresh the hashes above, rebuild with
  python build.py

Runtime notes (target runtime: CC:Tweaked = Lua 5.2 / Cobalt):
  * bit32 exists on CC:Tweaked (it is part of the Lua 5.2 standard library), which is the
    only supported path for the unpacker.
  * zzlib's _VERSION probe resolves to "< 5.3" on CC, i.e. require("inflate-bit32"); the
    injected require() answers both "inflate-bit32" and "inflate-bwo" with the vendored
    chunk, so neither branch can ever need a filesystem lookup.
  * Numbers are doubles on Lua 5.2, so zzlib's 32-bit little-endian arithmetic stays exact.
  * No Lua 5.2-removed APIs are used (unpack comes from table.unpack with a global
    fallback; there is no setfenv/getfenv/loadstring/module/math.log10/table.getn/
    math.mod), and no 5.3+ syntax (bitwise operators, //, math.type) appears anywhere in
    the bundle - build.py's luaparse check (Lua 5.1 target) enforces the latter.

Validation performed when this revision was added:
  * Python side: build.py re-reads every ZIP entry and compares it byte-for-byte with the
    stripped sources (the "载荷自检" line printed while building).
  * Real PUC Lua (Lua 5.4 via wasmoon) driving the generated ifm_bundle.lua against a
    minimal CC fs/shell mock:
        native bit path (standard bit32 semantics provided) .... 20/20 files byte-identical
        arithmetic fallback path (no bit32 and no bit) ......... 20/20 files byte-identical
  * fengari is deliberately not used for acceptance: its integers are 32-bit (JS bitwise
    semantics), so zzlib's little-endian reads overflow into negatives there and the CRC
    check fails spuriously. PUC Lua / CC:Tweaked are unaffected.
